steps.content: You find a dim emergency light and fasten it to your waist before setting out alone along the island's abandoned southern path.
The moss on either side has been eaten away by salt and decay, leaving the stone slick and treacherous. You advance with painstaking caution, each step measured.
A cellar key? I've been searching this island for two days. Never found a cellar.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Because you're an idiot.
Was that really necessary? It's childish.
What was the cellar for originally?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: A well. Connected to channels for the nine lighthouses. This was WhiteSands; we needed water.
Water? Then we could—

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: No. It's useless now.

You squeeze through the split structure of the chamber, ducking under a section of collapsed steel beams. Inside, the darkness is absolute, deep as the ocean abyss. The only remnants of light are shattered wires tangled in the iron frames overhead. The air is noticeably colder here, raising goosebumps on your skin.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: When the Black Tide hit, that was the first place to go.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: If it weren't for those channels, the filth might not have spread so damn fast.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: They sealed it after the contamination filled most of it in. No one's allowed back.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I won't stop you from going in. But don't blame me if you wake up the things sleeping down there.
"The things"?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Tide Crawlers. The beasts that crawl ashore at night. They're quiet on the seafloor during the day... but start clanging metal next to their ears, and see what happens.
I'm not that stupid.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Really? Couldn't tell.
You're really... Never mind.

Heeding Ceto's warning, you pick your way forward, avoiding loose debris and the soft, rotting wooden planks that sag under their own damp weight. The stagnant water in the cellar isn't deep, but its cold bites to the bone. As you reach the mouth of the passage, you instinctively pull your collar tight and hold your breath.
You said it was sealed. Can those things still get up through the cellar?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: People weren't supposed to go down, but there were always exceptions. Herbert did.
Who's Herbert?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: He took over as captain after Fynn died. Another keeper... Why am I even telling you this?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Anyway, that toolbox you're looking for... is down there.
What about Herbert... what happened to him?

Following Ceto's instructions, you fit the key into the iron door leading below. As you descend the stairs, the air grows thick and oppressive. The cellar walls weep with humidity, blanketed in a sickly moss, and the stench of sulfur and blood hangs heavy—a foul perfume of decay and corroding metal.

At the passage's end, a rear exit has been hastily barricaded. The heavy door is reinforced from the inside with crisscrossed steel beams, but a small rift has been forced open at the bottom. A dark, indistinct shape partially blocks the opening.
The putrid stench intensifies, emanating directly from this dark mass. You instinctively cover your mouth and nose, your breath catching in your throat.
The shadow begins to resolve into a vaguely recognizable form. A cold dread washes over you as a horrifying suspicion solidifies.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What happened... You already know the answer. Why ask?
[Red Flash with Horror Sound Effect] [Portrait: Dead Herbert]
It is a human corpse. Or, more precisely, half of one.
The right half soaks in the Black Tide, his remaining skin a grotesque map of complete mutation.
The left half remains inside the cellar, the hand locked in a death grip around a hydraulic cutter, frozen in the desperate act of trying to sever his own body in two.
A rusted toolbox lies fallen at his feet.
[Flashback] [Inside the Lighthouse]

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Where's Herbert? It's his shift.

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Ceto! It's "Captain" now. Don't be so disrespectful to the new captain of the lighthouse keepers.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You're loud.

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Miles, look at her! What happened to make her like this?

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: Heh, has our little Ceto ever been any other way? That's just her character.

steps.speaker: Sienna
steps.content: Ughhh, I give up! No one can handle her but Fynn, anyway!
The name hung in the air, a ghost of someone already gone. In the stiff silence that followed, Miles scratched his head.

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: Oh, right. Herbert said we're running low on Hypercubes. Soon we won't be able to suppress those weapons. He went to look for more.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Where would he even find more... Wait. He didn't go to—

steps.speaker: Miles
steps.content: The southern cellar. Said he had it under control.
[Flashback] [Cellar]

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: What are you doing here?! It's too dangerous!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You said you had it under control!
Young Ceto stood bewildered before Herbert, who was trapped in the doorway. Her mind had gone completely blank.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: I did... I almost made it. I just pried open a small gap. Look, right behind that door. Those blue, shining cubes... the things that would stop your nightmares. I just needed a little more time. But the Tide Crawlers... they found me first.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm not a child anymore! I know what those cubes are!

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Yes... You're not a child anymore. You're stronger than any of us. You can do many things that we can't. Our impressive little Ceto... could you do one last thing for me?
Herbert looked at the bewildered child and, summoning all his strength, extended his one movable hand to point at the dagger at her waist—the one Fynn had given her.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Help me... find peace.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What are you talking about?! I'll get you out... I'm getting you out of here!

Forcing herself to look away from his body, ravaged and festering from the monsters' feeding, Ceto's eyes fell upon the hydraulic cutter still hanging from his shoulder, fused with his corruption-riddled flesh. But she could barely see anyway; her tears had already blurred her vision.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: Don't cry. You can't afford to. There won't be any more Hypercubes to help you. From now on, you'll have to suppress the weapon's power all by yourself. Your emotions... they'll become a weakness your blade will exploit.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Stop lecturing me! Push! We'll weld the door shut, and you'll be fine!

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: I know... you never really accepted me as your captain. I'm not like you and Fynn. I can't command great power. I'm just an old logistics officer... who couldn't even complete his final task...
[End of Flashback] [Seaside]

The little girl from the past has grown up. Now, Ceto lies alone beneath the lighthouse, staring at the overcast sky as these memories surface. Not a single tear falls, yet she still lacks the courage to return to that place with the person from DisCity.
So, did you finally "help" him?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: He was the one who helped me.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: His blood quieted my blade like nothing else ever had.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: He told me... if it hadn't been for Fynn, he never would have agreed to let me grow up with the lighthouse keepers. He said...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: He said if I could really lead everyone out alive, he'd get to see his daughter again.

steps.speaker: Herbert
steps.content: I'd give anything to go home one last time... My girl would be your age by now...

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: After that, we sealed the contamination with rows of steel bolts. We left Herbert inside. He was the last captain of the lighthouse keepers.
[Cellar]

You carefully pick up the toolbox, and for a moment, everything seems to be going smoothly. Then you glance up and see it: the straps that once secured the lighthouse keeper's uniform to Herbert's remains now hang loose in an undignified slump.

After a moment's hesitation, you set the toolbox down and crouch to restore some final dignity to the man. But as your fingers near the fabric, the hydraulic cutter lodged in his body clatters suddenly to the floor, its jaw gaping ominously toward the sealed-off Black Tide.
You were the finest of lighthouse keepers. Your child would be proud of you.
You offer a silent prayer to the poor soul, but as you turn to go, the hydraulic cutter lodged in his body clatters suddenly to the floor, its jaw gaping ominously toward the sealed-off Black Tide.
[Sound Effect with White Flash]
Following the direction, your heart stops. Behind Herbert's remains, thousands of crimson eyes have slid open, fixed on you with chilling hunger.
Whether coincidence or final warning, the cutter's message is clear—
<color=#dg1f1f><size=50>RUN!</color></size>
